newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia bourse market capitalisation doubles in H1.
newsitem.headline: Zambia bourse market capitalisation doubles in H1.

text.p: Zambia's three-year-old Lusaka Stock Exchange (LuSE) has doubled its market capitalisation in the first six months of this year, making it the fastest growing exchange in sub-Saharan Africa, an official said on Monday.
The LuSE index has risen to 219.67 on June 27 from 100 on January 2.
By June 20, when the index stood at 199.36, it had risen 93 percent in dollar terms, exchange general manager Charles Mate told Reuters.
Market capitalisation had increased to U.S.$456 million in June from U.S.$231 million in January.
Mate said he believed the market's growth had been propelled by the country's privatisation programme.

"We believe the LuSE market to date is the best-performing sub-Saharan market and has significant room for growth and expansion, driven by Zambia's highly regarded and aggressive privatisation programme," he said.
Other exchanges on the continent had recorded markedly lower growth so far this year, Mate said.
"As at May, the Zimbabwe exchange had grown by 17 percent, the Botswana exchange by 25 percent and the Kenyan exchange by 4.75 percent," he said.
The Namibian exchange had risen 15.1 percent, while the Nigerian exchange had increased by 16.5 percent.
Last week, traded volume on the Lusaka Stock Exchange increased twelve-fold, mainly as a result of heavy turnover in Chilanga Cement.
The exchange said total traded volumes surged to 6.3 million shares valued at 748.3 million kwacha, compared with 563,492 shares valued at 22.7 million kwacha in the previous week.
Chilanga Cement rose 22.5 kwacha to close at 130 kwacha, on traded volume of 5.5 million shares valued at 713.6 million kwacha.

Mate said the Lusaka market's growth had been boosted by its trading system, which he described as the most modern in sub-Saharan Africa in terms of clearing and settlement procedures and market regulation.
"We believe our modern clearing facilities and procedures place us a step well ahead of other sub-Saharan markets," he said.
